localProtections.antiDiscriminationText: Under federal law, housing and employment discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity is unlawful.
localProtections.lede: Do additional legal protections exist for the LGBTQ community at the state level in New York? Do source of income protections exist for me at the state level in New York?
localProtections.attributionCopy: LGBTQ Legal Protections updated by Movement Advancement Project

description.text:
If local legal protections do not exist in your state, you are still protected under federal law. 

 

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) extended federal housing and employment discrimination protections to include the LGBTQ community in 2021. This makes housing and employment discrimination based on sexual  orientation and gender identity unlawful. 

 

If you believe you've experienced discrimination when searching for housing, you can contact a local fair housing organization.

body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.
